title: A fast unto death redrew India's map
sources: NCERT Class 12, Politics in India since Independence, ch. 1

quiz.q: Who chaired the States Reorganisation Commission?
quiz.why: Right. Fazl Ali chaired it; Panikkar and Kunzru were members.

review.note: Written and voiced by Claude (AI voices, Kokoro), 8 Nov 2026. Not yet checked by a subject or Hindi editor. Check every number and date against the listed sources.

lines.say: In 1952, a man fasted for a Telugu-speaking state, and died.
Within four years, India's map was redrawn by language.

beats.say: In 1952, a man fasted for a Telugu-speaking state, and died. Within four years, India's map was redrawn by language.

lines.say: Potti Sriramulu died after a 56-day fast in December 1952.
Andhra State was formed in 1953. And the States Reorganisation Act followed in 1956.

beats.say: Potti Sriramulu died after a 56-day fast in December 1952. Andhra State was formed in 1953. And the States Reorganisation Act followed in 1956.

lines.say: Based on the Fazl Ali Commission's report,
the Act created 14 states and 6 union territories.

beats.say: Based on the Fazl Ali Commission's report, the Act created 14 states and 6 union territories.

lines.say: Leaders feared language states would break the country.
For Mains, argue that they largely did the opposite.

data.text: Many feared language would divide India. It mostly made the union stronger.
